Subject: Quick question on per-token ladder behavior at breakpoints

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of specific questions before we can move to an LOI. We run a traffic pattern that is very spiky (monthly end-of-month reports) and we want to understand two things about your per-token ladder: 

1) If we commit to a tiered monthly commit (e.g., 5M -> 25M -> 75M tokens), how is the customer billed when a single month crosses more than one breakpoint? Do you apply marginal pricing per token above each breakpoint or a blended average across the whole month?

2) If we do a multi-month smoothing clause (true-up/true-down), how do you handle months that would individually be cheaper under marginal but more expensive under blended? Any worked numeric examples would be super helpful.

I've attached our last six months of usage for reference. We want to model cases where a month spikes to ~40M tokens while quarterly average stays near 30M.

Appreciate any clarity you can provide today — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Nina

Hi Nina — thanks for the data and the clear framing. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Lauren (customer success / contract) so we can give a concrete, written example you can share with procurement.

Short answers up front: 
- We support both marginal and blended billing semantics; the customer chooses.
- For marginal, tokens above a breakpoint are billed at the marginal rate for that band. For blended, the total monthly volume is charged at the single blended average rate that corresponds to the final band.

I'll let Ben and Lauren add a worked example and propose language for a smoothing clause. If it's OK with you, we'll return a simple two-page pricing matrix + numeric scenarios (marginal vs blended) and a short addendum describing monthly true-up behavior.

Call options if needed: 4pm PT today or 10am PT tomorrow.

Nina / Evelyn — attaching the matrix (spreadsheet) with three scenario rows and per-token math. Key excerpts pasted below so it's quick to scan. Attachment: pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx

Scenario A — Marginal pricing (example bands):
Bands: 0-5M @ $0.008/token, 5M-25M @ $0.006/token, 25M-75M @ $0.004/token
Month usage: 40M tokens
Billing (marginal):
  0-5M -> 5,000,000 * $0.008 = $40,000
  5M-25M -> 20,000,000 * $0.006 = $120,000
  25M-40M -> 15,000,000 * $0.004 = $60,000
  Total = $220,000 (effective rate = $0.0055/token)

Scenario B — Blended pricing (same bands, final band wins):
Month usage: 40M tokens -> falls in 25M-75M band -> blended rate assigned = $0.004 (per token)
  Total = 40,000,000 * $0.004 = $160,000 (effective rate = $0.004/token)

Note the divergence: in this numeric example blended is cheaper for the single month. However, blended can be more expensive in months just over a lower breakpoint if the blended rate is above the marginal incremental cost. 

Smoothing / true-up mechanics (proposed):
- Monthly billing can use the customer-selected semantics (marginal or blended).
- Quarterly true-up: we calculate total tokens across the quarter. If the customer has overpaid relative to a committed quarterly tier, we credit on next invoice; if under, we invoice the difference.
- Transition protections: for customers with spikes, we can offer a 30-day transition cap so that the effective blended rate for the first spike-month is floored at the marginal outcome (i.e., we won't retroactively charge a higher blended-only number for a single transient spike). This protects customers from a one-off month pushing them into a higher blended band unexpectedly.

Margins / internal note: the 30-day transition cap is a bill-smoothing concession we can offer up to the Manager approval.

Ben

Nina — adding a couple practical contract-level notes and a transition matrix you can paste into procurement language. Also flagging optional smoothing add-ons we often include for customers with EOM spikes.

Transition matrix (one-line language for SOW):
- If Month M usage places the customer into Band B (based on that month's raw token count), billing will be applied according to the customer's selected semantics (marginal or blended). If Month M is > 150% of the customer's trailing 3-month average and the resulting blended charge would increase invoice by > 12% vs marginal billing for Month M, Redwood will apply the following protection: the customer will be billed at the lesser of blended or marginal for Month M, and the difference will be reconciled over the next 2 billing cycles (credit if overpaid, invoice if under).

Examples (quick):
- Quarterly smoothing: compute quarter total and settle to committed quarterly tier; credits or invoices applied on next month's statement.
- Monthly spike protection: single-month cap applies once per rolling 12-month period unless a separate capacity agreement is signed.

Operational notes: please send the preferred semantic (marginal or blended) in your LOI. If you want, we can default to marginal + optional blended opt-in after 6 months of steady usage.

Uploading a clean matrix to Drive now (link included). Ben — can you confirm manager-level approval to offer the 30-day transition cap for BrightApps?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
